title: Is log g(k) ~ c·k/log k for some constant c

problemStatement.plain: Is log g(k) ~ c·k/log k, where g(k) is the smallest n > k+1 with all prime factors of C(n,k) exceeding k?

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Reduced 4 axioms to 1 (gFunc_exists). gFunc now defined constructively via Nat.find. Properties derived as theorems.
builtItems: gFunc: axiomatized with gt, spec, minimal properties
choose_odd_of_allPrimesExceed: proved (C(n,k) must be odd for k≥2)
choose_3_1, choose_6_2, choose_4_2, choose_5_2: concrete computations
ErdosAsymptoticConjecture def: formal statement of log g(k) ~ c*k/log k
insights: g(k) = smallest n > k+1 such that all prime factors of C(n,k) exceed k
Known bounds: k^(1+c) < g(k) ≤ exp((1+o(1))k), with Konyagin lower bound exp(c(log k)²)
Conjecture: log g(k) ~ c·k/log k — places g(k) between polynomial and exponential growth
For k ≥ 2, the AllPrimesExceed condition forces C(n,k) to be odd (since 2 ≤ k)
Kummer's theorem: C(n,k) is odd iff no carries in binary addition of k and n-k — constrains valid n
g(3) = g(4) = 7 because C(7,3) = C(7,4) = 35 = 5*7 has no prime factor ≤ 4
Asymptotic conjecture formalized as ErdosAsymptoticConjecture using Filter.Tendsto and Real.log
The 4 axioms are structural (define gFunc via existence) — cannot be eliminated without formalizing Kummer theorem + CRT existence proof
4 axioms are structural (define g(k) noncomputably) not mathematical claims — appropriate
